question: A 19-year-old nulligravid woman comes to the physician because of irregular heavy menstrual bleeding since menarche at age 16 years. Menses occur at irregular 15- to 45-day intervals and last 7 to 10 days. She has also noted increased hair growth on her face. She has not been sexually active since she started taking isotretinoin for acne vulgaris 4 months ago. Her 70-year-old grandmother has breast cancer. She is 163 cm (5 ft 4 in) tall and weighs 74 kg (163 lb); BMI is 28 kg/m2. Pelvic examination shows copious cervical mucus and slightly enlarged irregular ovaries. If left untreated, this patient is at an increased risk for which of the following complications?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Irregular heavy menstrual bleeding" -> "Increased hair growth on face" -> "Irregular 15- to 45-day menstrual intervals" -> "Lasting 7 to 10 days" -> "Slightly enlarged irregular ovaries" -> "Copious cervical mucus" -> "Increased risk for endometrial cancer" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Isotretinoin use for acne vulgaris" -> "Not sexually active since starting medication" -> "Increased risk for endometrial cancer due to irregular menstrual bleeding and other symptoms" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Family history of breast cancer" -> "Increased genetic predisposition for breast cancer" -> "Increased risk for breast cancer in the patient" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with irregular heavy menstrual bleeding, increased hair growth, and irregularly enlarged ovaries, suggestive of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). PCOS is associated with anovulatory cycles, leading to unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium, which increases the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and subsequently endometrial cancer if left untreated.
